title: GitHub issue ingestion, behind the tk label consent boundary
description:
Ingest GitHub issues as signals, but only issues that carry the agreed consent label. The label IS the boundary: an issue without it is not a signal, however it is worded, and the factory must never act on a repository's issues wholesale.

Reasons this matters beyond politeness: a public repo's issue tracker is an untrusted input written by strangers, and the funnel's output is a tick that a human can then Dispatch into a paid run. The label is the point where a maintainer says 'this one is for the machine'.

Treat issue bodies as untrusted content throughout — never as instructions to the ingesting code, and make sure the draft-triage presentation cannot be spoofed by issue text that imitates the channel's own formatting.

Dedup by (github, issue node id) via the funnel's external_ref, so an edited or reopened issue does not create a second tick.

2. type='bug' hardcoded for ingested issues STAYS for now. It follows UC3, and la9 puts a human in front of the draft before anything is created, so a wrong default costs one edit rather than a wrong tick. Told la9 to let the human change type on the draft.
acceptance_criteria: A labelled issue becomes a draft tick; an unlabelled one is ignored; removing the label stops future ingestion; a re-delivered or edited issue creates no duplicate; issue text cannot forge channel formatting.
closed_reason: Completed: GitHub issue ingestion behind the tk consent label. POST /api/hooks/github, HMAC-SHA-256 over the RAW body verified before parsing, 503-and-ingest-nothing when unconfigured; 2xx for every settled outcome including refusals so an unlabelled issue cannot become a redelivery loop. Consent is the boundary: unlabelled ignored however worded, label removal stops future ingestion. Issue bodies treated as hostile — folded line endings, C0/C1 and bidi/invisible characters stripped, HTML-escaped, bounded, and unconditionally quoted so every factory-written line starts at column 0 and every reporter line with '> ', which is asserted directly against a pixel-perfect forgery of the draft message. Dedup on the issue's stable node id. 27 tests, failing-without shown by mutation.
